reviews.comment: This is by far the worst professor I've had at Texas A&M. His class ATMO 444 is extremely biased towards his own views and ultimately the subject he teaches  is worthless in life. He's extremely childish when he feels like students are disrespecting his class time and will call you out.
His teaching style always kept me super intrigued. If you missed attendance quizzes you could make them up with extra writing assignments which was super nice.

There is a LOT of reading for this class, but I never found it to be too daunting. I enjoyed his lectures more than anything; he's very real and straight up with the material, and I really liked that.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took him as a grad student. “Awful” doesn't do him justice. His PP slides weren't available till after class so you couldn't read what you were doing before class to come prepared. He didn't teach out of one text book. We had to “find our own”. The texts he did use were all in German. His slides were vague so they were useless. Never again.

Dr. Schade is very passionate and intelligent. He explained climate change science well in a small time frame. He's a picky grader and sometimes will tell students they're incorrect on subjective matters. Had to read a lot throughout the semester. Exams weren't bad, group project was easy.

Loved the content of this class, very interesting. 2 exams, no final, 1 group project (easy), 3 assignments, and Acadly quizzes (attendance grade, easy if you read the material). Wish Dr. Schade taught more classes, I thoroughly enjoyed this class and thought the material was very relevant and important. Take this class!

He's clearly interested in the subject material, which makes his lectures at least somewhat captivating, but his class is a MESS... he has no organizational skills and expects you to pick up the pieces.

Dr. Schade is very nice, but the class is difficult and confusing, especially for non-meteorology majors. Lecture goes by pretty slowly, and it can be very difficult to pay attention, but in-class quizzes meant you had to struggle through, rather than watch later at a faster speed. Made liberal use of breakout rooms.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Schade clearly knows what he's talking about and is great at answering questions, but the quizzes he gives in class as clicker quizzes, as well as weekly eCampus quizzes are very difficult and specific. This class was completely online, so he often uses breakout rooms. The 3 homeworks helped my grade but the weekly quizzes are 40% of your grade
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Schader has a tendency of being unorganized and it shows within his classes. Often, his own mistakes will penalize your grade. Be sure and read all given assignments as he has in class quizzes most days. The exams are straight forward and follow the in class lectures - so take notes. He allows you to use your notes during the exams!

Professor Schade clearly knows his stuff. He has a way of teaching that makes you care so much about the material that it becomes a priority to read the books he says and the articles he shares with the class! There are lots of in class quizzes through acadly based of those readings. Work for it and be involved in class and you'll do great!

Be prepared to work and pay attention in Dr. Schade's class. Tests, quizzes and homework assignments are all very specific, and it's often difficult to find information needed to complete assignments in lecture notes or the textbook. To do well, show up to class, take quizzes seriously, and understand the material in depth.

Dr. Gunnar is a horrible professor. He doesn't consider anyone but himself and will continuously tell you "that's not right" even when he admits he "doesn't know". Dr. Julie Loisel is much better. Avoid him at all costs.

Professor Schade is caring but at times I felt that it was more of an organic chemistry class than a atmospheric class. The extra credit opportunity was helpful. The quizzes were a bit difficult. Homework was comprehensive and a bit complex.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: this was an interesting class that is pretty discussion-heavy, but no forced participation. You have to go to class every time because he has graded clicker quizzes all the time. the tests are online and are not terrible. The writing assignments are straightforward and peer-graded. If you are interested in climate change, I recommend this class.

Lectures were boring but explained the book in detail. Book is needed for course. He made you work hard for the course as if it were your major and you simply didn't just need a easy science credit. Take Logan instead. Quizzes every week and there is a project
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's a nice professor. His lectures are powerpoints that are condensed versions of the book. Expect to answer 1-2 clicker questions based on material you should have read before class. He makes you write 3 essays in the semester +  take an online homework quiz once a week. Nothing is too difficult.  Even better if you have good memorization skills.

Lectures are super boring and you are expected to already know what he's talking about. Quizzes every week and a few papers that are not clear in the directions and are basically graded by peer reviews.

He is a very nice man, super passionate about what he is teaching which makes the class interesting. He only has one project at the end that was difficult only because we had to use excel & most of us have never used excel before. He was available for office hours all throughout the project, if you waited till the last minute it was your own fault.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He thinks he is teaching a graduate class, not an INTRO ONE.  He assigns very confusing work that he expects you to know how to do despite not going over it in class, he has iClicker questions in his powerpoints for attendance and grading, and he assigns quizzes on FRIDAYS at 3 in the afternoon.  Would never take a class with him again.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK
